decisions.reason: As the flagship extension of the firm's core cloud messaging capabilities, it remains highly aligned with existing knowledge and internal R&D, though its lower later visibility suggests some chance of being folded into a broader platform rather than kept as a distinct offer.

Document capture and recognition supports digital document workflows for business and public-sector clients, but because it sits somewhat farther from the firm's core messaging specialization and was not later prominent, it carries a meaningful rationalization risk.

Email and fax conversion still fits the firm's multichannel communications base and helps customers bridge legacy and digital processes, although the longer-term shift away from fax raises the chance of eventual withdrawal.

This fax optimization feature is easy for the firm to understand technically but is narrow, less strategically central to future cloud workflow growth, and the kind of peripheral legacy feature whose resources are better redeployed.

Multi-engine email virus scanning is closely related to the firm's secure email infrastructure and compliance-oriented customer base, so the firm has strong absorptive capacity to improve it and good reason to retain it.
